claims.statement: Adjunctive antibiotics should not be used routinely in ASUC without infection

claims.statement: Statement 128 (weak, very low): IBD patients receiving anti-TNF therapy should be counselled about risks and benefits of continuing treatment throughout pregnancy. For patients with active disease or high risk of relapse, it may be advisable to continue throughout. For those with inactive disease who wish to discontinue, it may be reasonable to stop at the start of the third trimester.
claims.evidence_excerpt: 97.7% agreement. Active IBD prior to conception is associated with poor pregnancy outcomes (premature delivery, low birth weight, spontaneous abortion). claims.evidence_excerpt: 97.7% agreement. The guideline cites multiple RCTs and meta-analyses showing no benefit of mesalazine over placebo for CD induction or maintenance. This is one of the strongest negative recommendations in the guideline, reflecting the consistency and quality of the evidence against mesalazine in CD.
